paras: The killing of Henry Foster was the shooting of a Black farmer who was called out of his house at night near Covington, Tennessee, in August 1881 and shot dead. The assassin escaped, and the case reached newspapers only as a one-sentence wire item from Memphis.

According to a Memphis dispatch dated August 10, Foster, described as "a colored farmer," lived five miles north of Covington. During the night someone called him out of his house and shot him to death. The dispatch said only that "the assasin escaped"; it named no suspect and gave no motive.
No report of an arrest, inquest or trial appears in the coverage.

The item ran in northern and southern papers on August 17, a week after the dispatch, mostly in news-summary columns. The Chicago Daily Tribune printed it with its Memphis dateline under the one-word head "ASSASINATED," while the Lancaster Daily Intelligencer placed it among its "Latest News by Mail." The National Republican and the Evening Critic of Washington carried the same words, and the Port Tobacco Times in Maryland repeated it in its "Notes" column on August 19.
None of these papers added comment, and none identified Foster's attacker or suggested a reason for the killing.

The versions differ on the night of the shooting: the dated Memphis dispatch said "last night," the night of August 9, while the Savannah Morning News said "Monday night" and the Port Tobacco Times "Tuesday night." Because August 9, 1881 fell on a Tuesday, the dated dispatch and the Port Tobacco Times agree, and the Savannah paper, which also printed the name as "Henry Forster," stands alone.

reader.title: Killing of Henry Foster
bases: The only report is a single wire brief that a Black farmer was called from his house and shot by one unnamed 'assassin' who escaped (A2, A1); it names no mob, band or motive, so the record's 'mob_assault' is not supported.
All four opened versions (A1, A2, A3, A6) and the two reprints (A4, A5) carry the same wording of one Memphis wire dispatch (A2), so there is no independent second report.

accounts.label: Memphis wire report
accounts.gist: Henry Foster, a colored farmer five miles north of Covington, was called out of his house at night and shot to death; the assassin escaped.

framing.detail: Ran as an unsigned one-sentence item in news-summary columns ('Latest News by Mail', 'Notes'), the Chicago Tribune under the one-word head 'ASSASINATED', with no comment on motive.

versions.value: 'last night' in a dispatch dated Memphis, Aug. 10 (i.e., Aug. 9)

conflicts.note: The dated Memphis dispatch is the best evidence; Aug. 9, 1881 fell on a Tuesday, which agrees with the Port Tobacco Times and not with the Savannah Morning News.
'Forster' appears only in one reprint of the same wire item and is likely a typesetting variant.

record_check.dossier: No mob is reported; a single unnamed 'assassin' shot Foster. Better coded 'other' (killing by an unknown individual).
1881-08-10 is the dispatch date; the shooting was 'last night', i.e. the night of Aug. 9 (one version says Monday night, Aug. 8).
Reported, but in one wire item only; no follow-up found.
